html:
Andreas Vesalius, born in Brussels in 1514, was a physician whose book On the Fabric of the Human Body, published in 1543, founded modern human anatomy.

For over a thousand years doctors had taught anatomy from the ancient Greek physician Galen, who had dissected mainly animals. Vesalius, professor at Padua, dissected human corpses himself and found that Galen was wrong in many places. His book, with detailed woodcuts, showed the body as it really is.

It appeared in the same year as Copernicus's book on the movement of the planets, and both are seen as starting points of the Scientific Revolution. Vesalius later became doctor to Charles V and his son. He died returning from a pilgrimage to Jerusalem. See Belgium and Copernicus.
sum: Andreas Vesalius, born in Brussels in 1514, was a physician whose book On the Fabric of the Human Body, published in 1543, founded modern human anatomy.
